attributes.name: Druva - Administrator Self Privilege Escalation
attributes.description: Detects a Druva administrator modifying their own account and changing their assigned administrator role. Self-directed role changes can indicate privilege escalation or misuse of administrative access.
author: Druva
false_positives: Authorized self-service privilege elevation under an approved administrative workflow.
Emergency or incident-response elevation explicitly approved by the organization.
Administrative testing in a non-production environment.
attributes.query:
FROM logs-druva.event-*
| WHERE druva.feature == "Admin Event"
    AND druva.event_type == "Administrator Updated"
    AND druva.security.control == "administrator_role"
    AND druva.security.previous_state == "role=Product"
    AND druva.security.current_state == "role=Druva Cloud"

| EVAL actor = TO_LOWER(
    COALESCE(
      TO_STRING(user.email),
      TO_STRING(user.id),
      TO_STRING(user.name)
    )
  )

| EVAL target_admin = TO_LOWER(
    COALESCE(
      TO_STRING(user.target.email),
      TO_STRING(user.target.name)
    )
  )

| WHERE actor IS NOT NULL
    AND target_admin IS NOT NULL
    AND actor == target_admin
attributes.note:
### Investigation guide

This rule detects a Druva administrator changing their own role from Product to Druva Cloud. Self-directed privilege elevation is particularly sensitive because the actor and target account are the same.

#### Investigation steps

- Identify the administrator and source IP associated with the role change.
- Confirm whether the administrator was authorized to elevate their own privileges.
- Review authentication activity before the elevation, including failed logins and impossible-travel alerts.
- Review privileged actions performed after elevation, including downloads, API credential changes, security-setting changes, protection changes, and recovery activity.
- Determine whether the elevated role was subsequently removed.
- Review other administrator-role changes performed by the account.

#### Response

- Revoke unauthorized elevated privileges.
- Investigate the administrator account for compromise or misuse.
- Review all privileged actions performed during the elevated period.
